nodes.description: The mechanistic centrepiece of the current genetics, and the model that explains why a dominantly inherited variant produces a sporadic-looking disease. Mice carrying a patient-derived EPHB4 kinase-domain missense change develop disordered angiogenesis and fail to build a proper artery-capillary-vein hierarchy, which is the developmental process this entry places at the top of its pathograph. The finding that matters most is conditional: the phenotype appeared only when a second-hit allele was also present. That converts incomplete penetrance from a shrug into a testable two-hit requirement, and it is the reason an inherited variant can sit silently in a parent.

A knockdown model used as a functional assay rather than as a phenocopy of the human malformation. Its value is the rescue design: wild-type human EPHB4 corrects the brain vascular defect and the truncated disease-associated form does not, which converts a candidate variant into a demonstrated loss-of-function.

nodes.description: The standard treatment, and mechanically the right one: it occludes the shunt itself, removing the low-resistance channel that drives every downstream consequence. Timing is the difficult judgement, balancing the cardiac emergency in a neonate against the technical and haemodynamic risks of intervening on a very small patient. Outcomes have improved substantially with it, but the long-term results remain worse than medium-term follow-up implies.

nodes.description: The upstream lesion, and the part of the picture that has changed most recently. Damaging variants in regulators of endothelial Ras signalling, with EPHB4 the most prominently enriched and RASA1, ACVRL1 and others also implicated, disturb the development of cerebral vasculature. Integrated analysis of exomes with cerebrovascular single-cell transcriptomes places the susceptibility specifically in developing endothelial cells, which locates the disease in a cell type at a developmental moment rather than in a vessel.

nodes.description: The dominant threat to the newborn. A large fraction of cardiac output passes through the shunt and returns to the right heart having done no work, so cardiac output must rise enormously to perfuse the body, and pulmonary blood flow rises with it. This is heart failure with a structurally normal heart, which is why the cardiac presentation can be baffling until the head is imaged.

nodes.description: The anatomical lesion. Primitive choroidal and subependymal arteries connect directly to the median prosencephalic vein of Markowski, with no intervening capillary bed, during the sixth to eleventh weeks of fetal development. The embryonic vein, which should have regressed, instead persists and dilates as the receiving limb of the shunt. Because no capillary bed intervenes, the circuit has very low resistance, and that single physical fact generates everything downstream.

nodes.description: The functional test behind the ACVRL1 assignment, built on the same rescue logic as the EPHB4 fish model. Depleting the two zebrafish acvrl1 paralogues produced massive dilation of a cranial vein, and the defect was corrected by wild-type human ACVRL1 messenger RNA but not by the patient Cys344Tyr form. That asymmetry is the whole argument: it shows the human variant is not merely rare but functionally deficient.
